_meta.what: Money people spend near their school or workplace (lunch, snacks, coffee, quick errands), per person per year, C$ 2025. The daytime crowd: it is spent where people are during the day, not near home.
_meta.status: SEED values from third-party surveys (older or US where no current Canadian figure was found). Each has a low-high range; the owner can correct any figure.
_meta.double_counting: For residents, this money is part of their household budget already: in the model it moves from near home to near school or work. Workers who live in other towns bring it in as new money.

high_school_student.basis: US teens spend about US$2,213 a year of their own money (Piper Sandler Taking Stock With Teens, fall 2025), about C$3,030; food is about 23-24% of it (Piper Sandler spring 2017 and spring 2023), about C$700; about half bought near school on school days (SEED).

elementary_student.basis: Children spend little of their own; parents buy coffee or a snack at drop-off and pick-up a few times a month (SEED).

worker.basis: 60% of Canadian workers buy lunch at least once a week, at about $8.30-9.30 (Visa Canada survey, about 2012); with restaurant prices up about 45% since, about $12.75; about 1.5 bought lunches a week among buyers over 46 weeks, about $530, plus coffee and snacks near work, about $115 (SEED).
